title: XGBoost model on EBV serology and blood markers identifies nasopharyngeal carcinoma
summary: An XGBoost model, the best of nine machine-learning models, used five markers (NTA1-IgA, VCA-IgA, Rta-IgA, platelets, lymphocytes) to identify nasopharyngeal carcinoma, reaching AUC 0.999 and 0.995 in internal training and validation (569 participants) and 0.956 in an independent external cohort of 160. The near-perfect internal AUC suggests an easy case-control separation, predictors are known EBV markers and the study is retrospective.
ai_technology: XGBoost (best of nine machine-learning models) on five EBV serology and blood markers
organization: People's Hospital of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region

evidence.unknown: Performance in a screening population; prospective performance; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A gradient boosting model separated nasopharyngeal carcinoma from non-carcinoma participants using serological markers.
